entries.source: read at CLASS level on the OWNER class, because a selector's presence somewhere in a release says nothing about the class that owns it: read at CLASS level, not from a name list: REVENANT_ROOT=<worktree> xmake l tools/corpus/objc-inventory.lua ~/.revenant/dyld/6.1.3/dyld_shared_cache_armv7 | grep -c '^class<TAB>MPMediaLibrary<TAB>' reads 0 at 6.1.3 and 0 at 4.3 (~/.revenant/dyld/4.3/dyld_shared_cache_armv7, 7751 lines: 7187 classes, 564 protocols). THE CONTROLS ARE IN THE SAME READS and are what make that zero mean something: the same command with MPNowPlayingInfoCenter reads 1 at 6.1.3 and 0 at 4.3 - same reader, same two files, a YES and a NO - and with MPVolumeView reads 1 at both. A reader that answered NO to everything would have produced this result for the wrong reason. The tab in the grep pattern is literal: a reader who types a space gets 0 for EVERY class and would conclude the whole release is empty, which is the same failure mode as the sign-prefixed selector columns facts/MediaPlayer/WholeCacheRead.md records. The 6.1.3 file holds 848 UIKit and 418 Foundation classes, so it is not blind to either framework. The release's whole-cache selector list (selectors_armv7.txt, 113981 DISTINCT NAMES) is a list of names and not per-class counts, so a one there says only that some class somewhere declares the selector; the per-class read above is what decides a member

THE CONTROLS ARE IN THE SAME READS and are what make that zero mean something: the same command with MPNowPlayingInfoCenter reads 1 at 6.1.3 and 0 at 4.3 - same reader, same two files, a YES and a NO - and with MPVolumeView reads 1 at both. A reader that answered NO to everything would have produced this result for the wrong reason. The tab in the grep pattern is literal: a reader who types a space gets 0 for EVERY class and would conclude the whole release is empty, which is the same failure mode as the sign-prefixed selector columns facts/MediaPlayer/WholeCacheRead.md records. The 6.1.3 file holds 848 UIKit and 418 Foundation classes, so it is not blind to either framework. The class arrived in 8.0 - tools/cache-index/first-rung.lua answers 8.0, the oldest HELD release that carries the name - and it is in neither cache, at either end. A CATEGORY ON A CLASS THE RELEASE DOES NOT HAVE compiles, links, and then never installs, which is why this row is absent and not implemented: the image would carry a category nobody can attach, and the row's own effect sentence - respondsToSelector: answers honestly - would be a claim about a class that does not exist. That is the same finding as ARKit's conformance-only category in ef271700, where the dylib had 0 occurrences of the name
